name: City building permit application review through issuance
summary: A property owner, contractor or architect applies to the city for a permit to alter, add to or build a commercial or residential building, and the city must confirm the plans meet the zoning, building, fire and public works codes before work starts. A permit technician checks the submittal and calculates fees, reviewers in each discipline mark up the plans, and the applicant answers a consolidated correction notice, usually more than once, before the plans are approved, final fees are paid and the permit is issued. Most of the elapsed time is waiting in reviewer queues and for the applicant's designers to revise drawings; about half the time is with the applicant. Incomplete submittals, the slowest discipline in each round and repeated correction cycles are the main sources of delay.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size to large US city building department with a permit center, building plan review, zoning, fire marshal and public works reviewers, using a permitting system with online submittal and electronic plan review.
baseline.notes: Covers permits that need plan review (roughly half of alteration permits in Seattle); over-the-counter or field-inspection permits, land use permits and inspections are out of scope. Step timings are calibrated to Seattle's 2019 to 2022 permit log for reviewed additions, alterations and tenant improvements.

unit_of_work: one building permit application that requires plan review (commercial or residential addition, alteration, tenant improvement or small new building)
trigger: The applicant uploads the application and plans to the city portal and requests intake.
end_state: The permit is issued with approved plans and conditions, or the application is withdrawn or expires.

volume.seasonality: Applications rise in spring and summer and before code changes or fee increases take effect; 2020 saw a dip and a shift to fully electronic submittal.

evidence.note: Seattle, a city of about 750,000, issued about 266 reviewed building permits a month in 2019 to 2022; 150 a month is the author's estimate for a mid-size to large city.

systems.name: Permitting and land management system with online portal
Fee schedule and building valuation table (spreadsheet)

steps.name: Applicant submits application and plans
steps.description: The applicant or the design professional uploads the application form, stamped drawings, site plan, energy and structural calculations and owner authorization to the city portal and requests an intake appointment.

error.defect_description: Missing sheets, unsigned drawings, wrong valuation or missing owner authorization.

evidence.note: Seattle describes online submittal and electronic intake appointments.

steps.name: Screen submittal for completeness
steps.description: At the intake appointment the permit technician opens the upload, checks the required forms, plan sheets, stamps, site plan and calculations against the submittal checklist for the permit type, confirms the parcel and zoning in GIS, and either accepts the application as complete or lists what is missing.

error.defect_description: An application missing a required document is accepted, which surfaces as a correction in plan review.

control.basis: State building permit law and locally adopted building code on application contents (for example Florida s. 553.792 requires notice of incompleteness within 5 business days)

next.condition: incomplete; applicant notified of missing items

evidence.note: Seattle usually takes in applications two to three weeks after upload. The 25% incomplete share is an estimate.

steps.name: Applicant supplies missing items
steps.description: The applicant gathers the missing documents, such as a signed owner authorization, a geotechnical report or a corrected site plan, and uploads them for a new intake check.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Verify valuation and calculate plan review fees
steps.description: The permit technician checks the declared construction value against the building valuation table (floor area times the rate for the occupancy and construction type), raises it if it is too low, calculates the plan review fee and other review fees, and posts the invoice in the permitting system.

error.defect_description: Wrong occupancy or construction type rate, so the fee is over or under charged.

control.basis: City fee ordinance setting permit fees from project valuation (building valuation data)

evidence.note: Seattle bases fees on project value with a building valuation data rule and collects about 75% at intake. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Applicant pays plan review fees
steps.description: The applicant pays the intake portion of the fees online; if payment does not arrive within the deadline the intake is cancelled and the application must be rescheduled.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: not paid; intake cancelled and not resubmitted

evidence.note: Seattle requires fees within 48 hours of the completeness determination. The 2% share is an estimate.

steps.name: Accept application and route to review disciplines
steps.description: The permit technician marks the application accepted, which starts the review clock, and creates review tasks for zoning, building, fire and public works as the scope requires, attaching the plan set to each.

error.defect_description: A required discipline is not routed, for example drainage review for added impervious area.

evidence.note: Seattle assigns reviews in the order submitted, based on review resources. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Assign reviewers and set target dates
steps.description: The plan review supervisor looks at each reviewer's queue and specialty, assigns the building review and confirms other disciplines, and sets target completion dates; complex or large projects go to senior examiners.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common workload practice in plan review offices; times are estimates.

steps.name: Zoning review
steps.description: The zoning reviewer checks the plans against the zoning code: permitted use, setbacks, height, lot coverage, floor area, parking and loading, landscaping and any conditions of earlier land use approvals, and records corrections on the plan markups.

error.defect_description: A setback or parking requirement is missed and found at inspection.

control.basis: City zoning ordinance (land use code) compliance review before building permit issuance

evidence.note: The queue wait for the first review round is set so the initial review round matches Seattle's median of 26 days (Computed by the author from the Seattle building permits open data log, 9,388 reviewed addition, alteration and tenant improvement permits issued 2019 to 2022.)

steps.name: Building code plan review
steps.description: The plans examiner reviews the drawings and calculations for occupancy, construction type, egress, fire-resistance ratings, structural design, accessibility and energy code, marks each deficiency with a code citation in the electronic plan set, and notes required special inspections.

error.defect_description: A code deficiency is missed and found at inspection, causing field rework.

control.basis: State building code act and locally adopted International Building Code or Residential Code: building official examines construction documents before a permit is issued

next.condition: commercial, multifamily or sprinklered work needs fire review

evidence.note: Reviews run in parallel with zoning, so the extra wait is small. Hands-on time and the 60% fire share are estimates.

steps.name: Fire code plan review
steps.description: The fire protection plans reviewer checks fire department access, hydrant distance, sprinkler and alarm requirements, hazardous materials and exiting against the fire code, and records corrections or approval.

error.defect_description: Fire access or sprinkler requirement missed.

control.basis: Locally adopted International Fire Code: fire code official review of construction documents

next.condition: site, drainage or right-of-way work needs public works review

evidence.note: Seattle lists fire department requirements for these permits. Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Public works and drainage review
steps.description: The public works engineer reviews site drainage and stormwater controls, driveway and curb cuts, work in the right of way and utility connections, and records corrections, often asking for a drainage report or a revised civil sheet.

error.defect_description: Drainage or right-of-way condition missed.

control.basis: City stormwater code and right-of-way ordinance (stormwater controls required under the city's Clean Water Act municipal stormwater permit)

evidence.note: Seattle may require drainage review under the stormwater code with hourly fees. Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Consolidate comments and issue correction notice
steps.description: Once every discipline has finished, the lead plans examiner checks that comments do not conflict, compiles them into one consolidated correction report and notifies the applicant, or records that all disciplines approved on first review.

error.defect_description: Conflicting comments from two disciplines sent to the applicant.

next.condition: all disciplines approved on first review

evidence.note: 12.4% of reviewed alteration permits needed one review cycle. Seattle waits for all reviews before the applicant may respond.

steps.name: Applicant revises and resubmits plans
steps.description: The applicant's architect and engineers answer each comment in the correction report, revise and cloud the drawings, sometimes ask the reviewer for a meeting, and upload a complete corrected plan set with responses.

error.defect_description: Incomplete response or a full plan set not uploaded.

next.condition: no response; application expires or is withdrawn

evidence.note: Applicant time per correction round: median 14 days, mean 30 (Computed by the author from the Seattle building permits open data log, 9,388 reviewed addition, alteration and tenant improvement permits issued 2019 to 2022.) The expiry share is an estimate because the log covers only issued permits.

steps.name: Check resubmittal for completeness
steps.description: The permit technician checks that the resubmittal has the full plan set, the responses embedded for each comment and correctly named files, then reopens the review tasks for the disciplines with open comments, or rejects the upload.

error.defect_description: A partial plan set is accepted.

control.basis: Department resubmittal standards: complete plan set with responses to every correction

evidence.note: Seattle will not review partial plan sets or uploads missing responses. The 8% rejection rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Re-review corrected plans (building)
steps.description: The plans examiner compares the corrected sheets with the earlier comments, checks that each correction is resolved and that the changes did not create new problems, and records remaining corrections or approval.

error.defect_description: A new issue introduced by the revision is missed.

next.condition: zoning, fire or public works comments also open

evidence.note: City time per re-review cycle median 12.5 days, mean 15.4; target two weeks. Branch shares reproduce the Seattle cycle distribution (mean 2.56 cycles).

steps.name: Re-review by other disciplines
steps.description: The zoning, fire or public works reviewer whose comments were open checks the corrected sheets for their items and records approval or further corrections, after which the lead examiner releases the result to the applicant.

error.defect_description: A discipline comment is closed without the fix.

evidence.note: Fire reviewer used as the representative role for zoning, fire and public works re-reviews; runs largely in parallel with s15. Shares are calibrated estimates.

steps.name: Approve plans and set permit conditions
steps.description: The plans examiner, acting for the building official, marks the plan set approved with the electronic stamp, lists required special inspections and deferred submittals, and records permit conditions from all disciplines.

error.defect_description: A condition from another discipline left off the permit.

control.basis: Building official approval of construction documents under the adopted building code; plans examiners hold state or ICC certification

evidence.note: Seattle plan review complete to ready to issue: median 1 day, p90 13 for reviewed permits. Hands-on time is an estimate.

steps.name: Check clearances and contractor license
steps.description: The permit technician checks that holds are cleared, such as utility capacity charges, impact or school fees, recorded covenants or health department approval, and verifies the contractor's state license and insurance in the state lookup.

error.defect_description: An unlicensed or lapsed contractor is listed on the permit.

control.basis: State contractor licensing law and city requirements for other agency clearances before issuance

evidence.note: Common permit center practice; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Applicant resolves holds
steps.description: The applicant pays an outside charge, obtains another agency's sign-off, records a required document or replaces the contractor, and notifies the permit center.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Calculate final fees and invoice
steps.description: The permit technician recalculates fees for any change in scope or valuation, adds hourly review charges, the issuance balance, inspection and technology fees, and posts the final invoice.

error.defect_description: Hourly review charges or a valuation change not billed.

control.basis: City fee ordinance: fees paid in full before permit issuance

evidence.note: Seattle collects the remaining fees before issuance. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Applicant pays remaining fees
steps.description: The applicant or contractor receives the final invoice notice, pays the balance online or by check, and the payment posting releases the permit for issuance.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Seattle ready to issue to issued: median 0 days, p90 10 for reviewed permits.

steps.name: Issue permit and release approved plans
steps.description: The permit technician issues the permit in the system, which generates the permit card and stamped approved plan set in the portal, notifies the applicant, and opens the inspection record for the field inspectors.

error.defect_description: Wrong plan set version attached to the issued permit.

evidence.note: Seattle issues permits and approved plans through the portal. Times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Incomplete submittal at intake
exceptions.description: The intake screen finds missing documents, the applicant uploads them and the application is screened again.

exceptions.name: Fire review required
exceptions.description: Commercial, multifamily or sprinklered work adds a fire protection plans review in each round.

exceptions.name: Public works and drainage review required
exceptions.description: Site work, added impervious area or right-of-way work adds a public works review and often a drainage report.

exceptions.name: Three or more review cycles
exceptions.description: The corrections are not fully resolved in the first resubmittal, so the applicant revises again and reviewers re-review.

exceptions.name: Resubmittal rejected at intake
exceptions.description: The corrected upload lacks the full plan set or the comment responses and is sent back before review.

exceptions.name: Major redesign
exceptions.description: The owner changes the project substantially during corrections, triggering a full review by every discipline and often added fees.

exceptions.name: Clearance hold before issuance
exceptions.description: An outside charge, another agency's sign-off or a contractor licensing problem holds the approved permit until the applicant resolves it.

exceptions.name: Application expires or is withdrawn
exceptions.description: The applicant stops responding to corrections or does not pay intake fees, and the application expires under the code's time limit or is withdrawn.

pain_points.description: Most permits go through two or more correction cycles, each adding about two weeks of applicant time and two weeks of City re-review.

evidence.note: Mean 2.56 cycles; only 12.4% approved on first review.

pain_points.description: The applicant cannot respond until every discipline has finished, so the slowest reviewer sets the pace of each round.
Intake appointments and completeness screening add weeks before the review clock starts, and incomplete submittals restart the wait.

evidence.note: Seattle usually takes in applications two to three weeks after upload.

pain_points.description: Fees are calculated by hand from valuation tables and hourly charges, with errors caught only at final invoicing or audit.

evidence.note: Common practice; no error rate was found.

sources.title: Building Permits (open data, dataset 76t5-zqzr)
sources.publisher: City of Seattle, Department of Construction and Inspections
sources.supports: Event log with applied, initial review complete, plan review complete, ready to issue and issued dates, review cycles and days out for corrections. Author's computation for 9,388 reviewed addition, alteration and tenant improvement permits issued 2019 to 2022: intake to issue median 80 days, p75 144, p90 263, mean 124; review cycles mean 2.56 (12.4% one cycle, 44.0% two, 27.4% three, 10.6% four, 3.5% five, 2% six or more); initial plan review median 26 days, p90 60; applicant time per correction round median 14 days, mean 30; City time per re-review cycle median 12.5 days, mean 15.4; 266 reviewed building permits issued a month; about half of alteration permits (50.6%) needed plan review, the rest were issued subject to field inspection. All reviewed commercial addition or tenant improvement permits: median 73 days, p90 236, 20% approved on first review.

sources.title: How Do You Get a Permit?
sources.publisher: City of Seattle, Department of Construction and Inspections

sources.title: Construction Permit: Addition or Alteration
sources.publisher: City of Seattle, Department of Construction and Inspections
sources.supports: Fees based on project value, about 75% paid at intake and the rest at issuance, plus hourly fees for drainage and geotechnical review; initial review target two to three weeks for simple and eight weeks for complex permits; drainage review under the stormwater code; fire department, transportation and utility requirements; multiple correction rounds possible.

sources.title: How to Respond to Review Comments
sources.publisher: City of Seattle, Department of Construction and Inspections
sources.supports: All reviews in a cycle must be complete before the applicant can respond; consolidated correction report; full corrected plan set required or it will not be accepted; target review time for corrected plans is two weeks.

sources.title: How Much Will Your Permit Cost?
sources.publisher: City of Seattle, Department of Construction and Inspections
sources.supports: Permit cost depends on project size, complexity and value of work, review hours, inspection and technology fees; Director's Rule on building valuation data used to implement the fee subtitle.

assumptions: Timings and branch probabilities are calibrated to Seattle's 2019 to 2022 log for reviewed additions, alterations and tenant improvements; Seattle is a large, busy department and smaller cities often review faster.

Seattle's clock starts at intake acceptance; the simulated cycle adds the pre-acceptance intake queue (about 10 days) and incomplete-submittal loops, so the simulated median is expected to be one to three weeks above the 80-day benchmark.

Discipline reviews run in parallel; the model lists them in sequence with the first-round queue wait on zoning and short extra waits on the others, so the initial round matches Seattle's 26-day median.
Re-review by zoning, fire or public works is represented by one step with the fire reviewer's role and cost.
Shares needing fire (60%) and public works review (50%), incomplete submittals (25%) and holds (15%) are estimates for a mix of commercial and residential work.
Expired and withdrawn applications (about 7%) are estimates, because the Seattle log covers issued permits only.

Hands-on review times (about 15 staff hours per permit including re-reviews) are estimates; they are consistent with plan review fees of several hundred to a few thousand dollars (Chicago median total fee $800).
Triangular distributions cannot match the long right tail of applicant correction times (Seattle median 14 days, mean 30 per round), so the simulated p90 is likely below Seattle's 263 days.
Volume of 150 reviewed permits a month and the staffing levels are estimates for a mid-size to large city.
Loaded costs use BLS May 2021 local government wages times about 1.9 (benefits factor 1.62 from BLS ECEC plus about 20% overhead).
The model code (IBC, IFC) text could not be opened during research; controls name the adopted codes, and evidence relies on Seattle's published process and Florida's statute.
